e08_data_race_send.title: Threads mutate a shared non-thread-safe container

pion.first_diagnostic: E_NOT_SEND: cannot capture non-Send value `hits` inside `spawn`
pion.fixit_sample: hint: wrap `hits` in `Mutex::new(...)` or transfer ownership with `move hits`

moonbit.note: MoonBit has no shared-memory threads; the bug class cannot be expressed (sequential analogue checked)

rust.first_diagnostic: E0499: cannot borrow `hits` as mutable more than once at a time
rust.fixit_sample: edit (MachineApplicable): to force the closure to take ownership of `w` (and any other referenced variable -> 'move '

go.note: compiles; only the runtime race detector (go run -race) reports it, and only on executions that interleave

e09_unhandled_result.title: Fallible call whose error is silently dropped

pion.first_diagnostic: E_UNHANDLED_RESULT: value of type `Result[Unit, String]` is silently discarded
pion.fixit_sample: hint: handle the Result with `match`, `?`, or explicitly discard with `let _ = ...`
pion.note: a Result in statement position is a compile error (E_UNHANDLED_RESULT); `let _ = ...` discards it explicitly

moonbit.first_diagnostic: 4122: Function with error is not allowed in `fn main`. You could use `fn main raise` to declare the main function with an error type.
moonbit.note: idiomatic MoonBit uses checked `raise`; calling a raising function without handling it is a compile error

rust.first_diagnostic: warning: unused `Result` that must be used
rust.fixit_sample: edit (MaybeIncorrect): use `let _ = ...` to ignore the resulting value -> 'let _ = '
rust.note: unused Result is a `must_use` warning, not an error

go.note: a discarded error return compiles silently (go vet has no errcheck)
